inline_comments.comment: `detectAgent()` returns `undefined` when no AI agent environment is detected—which is the normal state for every human developer doing a plain `git commit`. Calling `.name` on `undefined` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name')`, crashing the pre-commit hook entirely. The internal usage in `code/core/src/telemetry/detect-agent.ts` already handles this correctly by checking the result before accessing its properties. Fix with optional chaining: `detectAgent()?.name`.

`cd ..` chained with `&&` does not work portably on Windows (cmd.exe does not propagate directory changes across `&&`-joined commands). The pattern already used throughout this file for cross-directory invocation is `yarn --cwd <path> <script>`, e.g. `"i": "yarn --cwd .. i"`. Use `yarn --cwd .. fmt:check` here to be consistent and portable.

`importOrderSeparation` and `importOrderSortSpecifiers` are options from the `prettier-plugin-import-order` Prettier plugin—they are not recognised by oxfmt and will be silently ignored. This override block has no effect. If the intent is to disable import sorting for `.md`/`.mdx` files, check the oxfmt documentation for the correct option name, or remove these entries to avoid misleading future readers.

The formatter has re-indented the template-literal body, prepending 6 spaces of leading whitespace to each line of the error message string (e.g., `' It looks like…'`). Since the string is rendered via `.replaceAll('\n', '
')` into an HTML `

`, browsers collapse the leading spaces, so the visual regression is minimal. However, the raw string value has changed, and any non-HTML consumer (e.g., `console.log(message)`) would show the spurious indentation. Consider using a `dedent` helper or aligning the message lines to the left margin inside the template literal. Separately, the sibling change `

    ` → `
` on line 88 is a genuine HTML bug-fix worth calling out positively.

The file is missing a trailing newline (`\ No newline at end of file`). The same issue exists in `.vscode/extensions.json`. POSIX specifies that text files should end with a newline; without it, `git diff` marks the line, and some editors and tools behave unexpectedly.

The `lint` CI job now includes a standalone `'Format check'` step that runs `yarn fmt:check`, and the new `fmt` CI job (also defined in this file) independently runs the same `yarn fmt:check` command. For any workflow tier where both jobs are scheduled (e.g., `docs` and above per `scripts/ci/main.ts`), the full-monorepo format check runs twice. Consider removing the `'Format check'` step from `lint` and relying on the dedicated `fmt` job, or folding the `fmt` job into `lint` and removing the separate job.

general_comments.comment: The pre-commit behaviour has changed silently for human developers. The previous lint-staged configs in `code/package.json` and `scripts/package.json` always ran `oxfmt` (write/auto-fix mode) on staged files. The new root `.lintstagedrc.mjs` runs `oxfmt --check` (check-only mode) for anyone not in a detected AI agent environment, so a commit will fail if files are not already formatted. `AGENTS.md` documents the AI-agent path, but there is no mention in `CONTRIBUTING.md` or the hook itself that human developers now need to configure editor-level format-on-save or run `yarn fmt:write` manually before committing. A brief note in `CONTRIBUTING.md` would prevent unexpected friction.

The code examples in `code/lib/eslint-plugin/docs/rules/*.md` have been reformatted from single quotes to double quotes (e.g., `'Button'` → `"Button"`). The project's formatter config has `"singleQuote": true`, and these Markdown docs are the canonical reference for eslint-plugin users who copy the examples verbatim. Because `code/lib/eslint-plugin` is now listed in `ignorePatterns`, oxfmt will not touch these files going forward, making the double-quote style permanent unless manually reverted. The examples should use single quotes to match the project's JavaScript convention.
